data.raw_text:
Balikatan-2026 Exercise

In the Balikatan-2026 exercise (April 20 to May 8), more than 17,000 troops were deployed to Itbayat Island (Batanes Province, Philippines), where they trained to operate in conditions closely resembling combat.

The exercise focused primarily on potential conflict scenarios in the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait.

The main contributors were US forces (approximately 10,000 personnel), along with Philippine (approximately 5,000), Australian (approximately 400), and Japanese (up to 1,400) troops. Canada, France, and New Zealand participated fully for the first time.

The exercise included combat drills in the South China Sea and near Taiwan, as well as coastal defense exercises in northern Luzon. Despite official statements denying any "exercises near Taiwan," the actual geography of the exercise suggests preparations for a potential regional conflict.

 Among the weapons being used is the US Typhoon missile system, which has been deployed to the archipelago since 2024, previously drawing sharp criticism from China.

Japan, for its part, plans to use its Type 88 anti-ship missile to destroy a simulated maritime target.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiajun criticized the exercise, saying that participating countries were "playing with fire" and contributing to increased tensions in the region.

Beijing traditionally views such exercises as attempts at deterrence and military pressure.

Philippine President F. Marcos previously indicated that in the event of a conflict over Taiwan, his country would be forced to participate due to its geographical proximity.

Overall, Balikatan-2026 demonstrates a shift from formal exercises to practical training for large-scale conflict scenarios with US allies in the Asia-Pacific region.
